messages:
jessica: Customer (Acme Analytics) flagged a negative credit line on their Azure Marketplace invoice, looks like a -$2,400 line under 'Marketplace Adjustments'. Can we confirm what triggered that?

samir: ugh, lemme pull the invoice id and usage. invoice id INV-AZ-2026-0132, marketplace subscription id MSUB-99887. They say dashboard usage (tokens) ≠ marketplace line item tokens.

mike: Can you paste the Redwood usage export for the tenant? I'll compare to the marketplace CSV.

jessica: rctl usage export --tenant acme-tenant --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-02-28 --format csv -> attached excerpt:
account,model,token_count
acme-tenant,gpt-2.7,412345
acme-tenant,embedding-small,23456
TOTAL, ,435801

samir: Azure Marketplace report (from billing portal) shows:
Subscription,LineItem,TokenCount,Amount
MSUB-99887,compute-usage,912345,$9,123.45
MSUB-99887,marketplace-credit-offset,-476544,-$4,765.44
NET TOKENS: 435801 -> amount net -$2,400 (approx)

lili: Noting that marketplace sometimes applies partner credits or reconciliations as negative line items. But the token count on their MSUB row is much larger than our raw tokens (912k vs 435k). Looks like double-attribution: two upstream accounts maybe aggregated?

billing-bot: Invoice INV-AZ-2026-0132 posted 2026-03-02 17:03 UTC. Adjustment code: AZ-MP-ADJ-2026-02-18.

amarketplace-support: We see MSUB-99887 used aggregated meter data from both MSUB-99887 and MSUB-99888 during the billing window. The partner mapping shows both SKUs attributed to the partner connector.

mike: aha — customer has a sibling subscription (MSUB-99888) used for internal staging. Our tenant mapping (tenant -> subscription) currently points both staging and prod to the same tenant id in our marketplace attribution table. That would double-count tokens on the Marketplace side, then Azure applied a credit to reconcile.

jessica: can we confirm mapping? rctl tenant show-mapping --tenant acme-tenant -> marketplace_subscriptions: MSUB-99887, MSUB-99888 (alias present). This aliasing was added by SRE during onboarding to enable org-level billing.

samir: so marketplace charged gross (912k tokens), then partner credit offset (-476k) to split to other tenant, netting back to our raw 435k. But invoice shows a negative money line because the credit was applied to the same subscription. Customer sees that as unexpected negative charge.

lili: Proposed fix: 1) update our attribution so staging subscription maps to staging-tenant (separate) OR 2) ask Azure to reallocate the credit line to MSUB-99888 instead of MSUB-99887. Which is faster?

jessica: Customer would prefer we get Azure to reallocate the credit. I filed a case with Azure support (case AZ-452190). Linking to support ticket: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/Case/AZ-452190

amarketplace-support: We can request reallocation but need evidence: invoice, usage export, and the marketplace subscription GUIDs for both subs.

mike: I'll package evidence. attaching small CSV snippet and tenant mapping screenshot.

billing-bot: Note: Manual adjustment windows for marketplace credits are 30 days from invoice date — if not fixed before next payment run, customer will see the negative adjustment on their statement.

customer-ops: Communicated to Acme: "We're investigating; this is a billing attribution issue between your staging and production subscriptions. We've requested Azure to reallocate the credit. No net overcharge to you — the negative line is a bookkeeping artifact. We'll update you once Azure confirms reallocation." :pray:

samir: Follow-up action items: (1) Mike: send evidence to Azure case (done) (2) Billing: hold any autopay for INV-AZ-2026-0132 until Azure confirms reallocation (jessica to coordinate) (3) Engineering: update tenant->subscription mapping docs to avoid auto-aliasing (mike + lili).

jessica: holding autopay flagged with finance (DO NOT AUTO-PAY flag set).

mike: created internal issue: INT-7621 "prevent marketplace aliasing causing double attribution" and added a short-term guard (ignore alias when subscription has 'staging' tag).

lili: I'll draft a KB article so CS can explain negative marketplace adjustments to customers: steps to reconcile and why it appears.

jessica: customer notified. Azure responded to case: "We've accepted the reallocation request and will post an adjustment by 2026-03-05." I'll update when invoice is reissued. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: closing loop with Acme: thanks for patience, reallocation confirmed pending posting.

samir: marking thread resolved when credit reallocation is posted and invoice reissued.

jessica: thx team.
